field.label: Enable Health Endpoint
field.comment: Enable or disable the /pulsar/health endpoint

field.label: API Key
field.comment: Auto-generated during installation. Copy this key into your Pulsar dashboard. To regenerate, clear the field and save. Requests must include header: X-Pulsar-Key: your-api-key

field.label: Cron Status
field.comment: Check cron job health and stuck jobs

field.label: Cron Pending Jobs Warning Threshold
field.comment: Number of overdue pending jobs before status becomes degraded (default: 200). Increase for busy stores with frequent imports.

field.label: Cron Failed Jobs Warning Threshold (24h)
field.comment: Number of failed cron jobs in 24 hours before status becomes degraded (default: 5)

field.label: Indexer Status
field.comment: Check indexer health and invalid indexes

field.label: Cache Status
field.comment: Check cache types and invalidation status

field.label: Database Status
field.comment: Check database connectivity

field.label: System Status
field.comment: Check PHP version, disk space, and memory

field.label: Search Engine Status
field.comment: Check Elasticsearch/OpenSearch cluster health and catalog index status

field.label: Message Queue Status
field.comment: Check message queue depth, failed messages, and consumer health

field.label: Deploy Mode Status
field.comment: Check deploy mode, maintenance status, and compilation state

field.label: Redis Status
field.comment: Check Redis connectivity and memory for session, cache, and page cache

field.label: Log Health Status
field.comment: Check log file sizes, debug logging, and error report accumulation

field.label: Admin Security Status
field.comment: Check failed login attempts, locked accounts, and 2FA status

field.label: Config Hygiene Status
field.comment: Check for production misconfigurations (template hints, minification, etc.)

field.label: SSL Certificate Status
field.comment: Check SSL certificate validity and expiry for the store base URL

field.label: Order Pipeline Status
field.comment: Check for stuck orders and payment failures

field.label: Capture Reconciliation (shipped but not captured)
field.comment: For deferred-capture flows (authorize → fulfil → capture on invoice/shipment, e.g. German "capture on invoice", Mollie/Klarna manual capture, or an ERP connector like PlentyONE). Flags open orders that were authorized/fulfilled but never captured — goods out, money never collected, authorization expiring. Works even when fulfilment happens in a connector with no Magento shipment. Leave off unless your store captures at or after fulfilment.

field.label: Deferred-Capture Payment Methods
field.comment: Optional. Comma or newline separated payment-method patterns that use deferred capture (e.g. mollie, klarna). Matched as a substring of the order's payment method. Used as evidence that an uncaptured order should have been captured; leave blank to rely on shipment/authorization evidence alone. Set this if your gateway doesn't record a Magento authorization transaction.

field.label: Capture Window (days)
field.comment: Authorization lifetime used to compute the capture deadline shown on each order (default: 28, ≈ Klarna/Mollie manual capture).

field.label: Warning Age (days)
field.comment: Order age (from creation) at which an uncaptured order becomes degraded (default: 7)

field.label: Critical Age (days)
field.comment: Order age at which an uncaptured order becomes critical — set a few days below the capture window so you act before the authorization expires (default: 21)

field.label: Integration Status
field.comment: Check API integrations and OAuth token health

field.label: PHP-FPM Status
field.comment: Check PHP-FPM process pool saturation. Requires pm.status_path = /status in your php-fpm pool config.

field.label: PHP-FPM Status URL
field.comment: URL to the PHP-FPM status page (default: http://localhost/status?json)

field.label: Media Integrity Status
field.comment: Scan pub/media/ for PHP webshells and suspicious file accumulation in upload directories

field.label: Upload Endpoint Status
field.comment: Monitor access logs for automated POST requests to file-upload endpoints

field.label: Access Log Path
field.comment: Absolute path to the web server access log. Leave empty to auto-detect common locations (/var/log/nginx/access.log, etc.)

field.label: Database Size Status
field.comment: Monitor total database size and largest tables. Results are cached for 24 hours.

field.label: Log Error Monitoring
field.comment: Parse exception.log and system.log for CRITICAL/ERROR entries and report unique error signatures. Uses incremental reading (only new content since last check).

field.label: Known-Noise Ignore Patterns
field.comment: Optional. One pattern per line (not comma-separated — log messages contain commas). Any CRITICAL/ERROR whose message contains one of these (case-insensitive substring) is dropped before it counts toward status — for log lines you've triaged as benign. No wildcards needed: a substring matches anywhere, so Could not acquire lock for cron job: plenty_ silences all plenty_* lock warnings. Suppressed entries are tallied as suppressed_count in the health payload.

field.label: Content Integrity Status
field.comment: Scan core_config_data head/footer HTML and CMS block/page content (all scopes) for injected skimmer / obfuscated JavaScript. Flags a compromise distinct from downtime.

field.label: Trusted Script Hosts
field.comment: Extra hostnames allowed in <script src> within stored content (comma or newline separated), beyond the built-in list and your store's own domain. An unrecognized external script is reported for review, not flagged as compromised.

field.label: Transactional Email Monitoring
field.comment: Detect sales confirmation emails (order/invoice/shipment/creditmemo) that Magento has given up on: with asynchronous sending, email_sent reaching 0 means every retry attempt was used; with synchronous sending, an unsent flag after the grace period means the send failed and will not be retried. Still-retrying documents are reported separately and do not affect status.

field.label: Applied Security Patches
field.comment: Inventory security patches applied to this store (composer patches, git apply, archived .patch files) and verify each is still present in the live code. Pulsar uses this to suppress security advisories for CVEs you have already patched, and alerts if an applied patch disappears (e.g. wiped by a composer install).

field.label: Patch Detection Mechanisms
field.comment: Which mechanisms to read for applied patches. Leave all selected unless a source produces noise for your setup.

field.label: Patch Directories
field.comment: Directories containing archived .patch/.diff files, relative to the Magento root (comma or newline separated). Leave empty to use the default: patches/

field.label: Checkout Funnel Monitoring
field.comment: Measures how many carts reach a chosen shipping method and how many of those become orders, and compares the trailing window against the store's own baseline. Catches the "site is up, checks pass, but customers quietly give up at the shipping step" class of incident — an age gate, carrier rate call or address validator failing for a subset of shoppers. Reads quote, quote_address and sales_order only; results are cached (5 min window / 6 h baseline).

field.label: Window (hours)
field.comment: Trailing period whose conversion is compared with the baseline (default: 24). Shorter windows react faster but need more traffic.

field.label: Baseline (days)
field.comment: How much history before the window forms the baseline (default: 28). Keep it below your quote lifetime (Sales › Checkout › Quote Lifetime, default 30 days) or the baseline shrinks.

field.label: Minimum Carts per Window
field.comment: Below this many carts in the window the collector reports healthy with a note instead of judging conversion (default: 50).

field.label: Degraded at Relative Drop (%)
field.comment: A stage becomes degraded when its conversion rate is at least this much below baseline, relative (default: 10 — e.g. 78% → 70%), and the drop is statistically significant (z ≥ 2).

field.label: Critical at Relative Drop (%)
field.comment: A stage becomes critical at this relative drop (default: 25 — e.g. 78% → 58%) with z ≥ 3.

group.label: Synthetic Checkout Traffic
group.comment: Pulsar's checkout flow adds a product to cart as a fresh guest and, with the shipping step enabled, types a fixture address. Every request of a run carries the X-Pulsar-Synthetic header and every quote it touches is tagged with the shopper email pulsar+<site id>@synthetic.byte8.io. Those quotes are kept out of the Checkout Funnel collector and deleted by cron. Exclude the same address in your marketing automation (Klaviyo, Mailchimp, Dotdigital abandoned-cart flows) and analytics. Developers: inject Byte8\Pulsar\Api\IsSyntheticRequestInterface to skip third-party calls (age verification, fraud scoring, ERP sync) for synthetic runs.

field.label: Delete Synthetic Quotes
field.comment: Hourly cron removes quotes carrying the synthetic shopper email once they are older than the age below (default: Yes).

field.label: Delete After (hours)
field.comment: Minimum age since the quote was last updated (default: 1, max 168). A run never lasts more than a few minutes.

field.label: Enable Signature Feed
field.comment: Pull updated content-integrity detection signatures from Pulsar hourly, so new skimmer/zero-day patterns are detected without a module update. Last-known-good is kept if the feed is unreachable.

field.label: Feed URL
field.comment: Full URL of the Pulsar signature feed, e.g. https://pulsar.byte8.io/signatures/bundle. Leave empty to disable pulling.

field.label: Feed Token
field.comment: Shared bearer token for the feed (the SIGNATURE_FEED_TOKEN configured on pulsar-server). Stored encrypted.
